title: Compact causal stamp and deadline-hint middleware for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight, backwards-compatible middleware for Redwood language SDKs that attaches a compact causal stamp and an optional deadline-hint to outbound requests. This enables the serving runtime and edge proxies to make latency-aware routing and early-shedding decisions without inflating header sizes or requiring full baggage propagation. The middleware must be pluggable across HTTP/gRPC/WS, be opt-out by default, and preserve compatibility with existing trace/span headers.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware emits a compact causal stamp header (R-Stamp) on outbound requests in Node/Python/Go
A deadline-hint header (R-Deadline) can be attached optionally and interpreted by runtime for soft-shed decisions
Header encoding fits within 32 bytes (typically 12-20 chars) to avoid MTU/path issues
Middleware integrates with existing tracer hooks so spans are correlated without requiring full baggage transfer
Metrics emitted for issued stamps, applied deadline hints, and client-side sheds
Integration tests demonstrate interoperability with existing propagation formats and fall back when peer does not understand headers
technical_notes: Causal stamp format: 10-12 character base62 compact id derived from 16b random + 2b epoch, plus 1 checksum char
Deadline-hint: single integer representing remaining time budget in ms (R-Deadline header). Optional; omitted when SDK caller uses streaming or non-blocking patterns
Encoding/validation: middleware includes a lightweight CRC8 to reject malformed stamps without full parse cost
Language SDK changes scoped to middleware layer only; tracer integration uses existing trace_id/span_id linkage when available
Header names: 'x-rd-stamp' and 'x-rd-deadline' (lowercase for proxy friendliness). Both are additive and ignored by legacy services
Placement: should run before retry/backoff wrappers so the original client budget is visible downstream
Metrics: counters for r_stamp_issued, r_deadline_applied, r_client_shed_count, r_header_bytes_saved (estimate), and histogram of applied-deadline-vs-observed-latency
Security: stamps do not encode PII or secrets. Stamps are opaque and rotate per-request. Security review required for potential fingerprinting risk
Tracing compatibility: when an existing trace header (traceparent/ot-tracer) exists, middleware links causal stamp as an attribute rather than replacing propagation headers
Transport: support for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSocket tunnel (fallback to metadata on gRPC)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 5% of SDK traffic): enable flag 'causal_stamp.deadline_hint' for internal test orgs. Monitor r_client_shed_count and overall 95p latency
Phase 2 (canary 25%): open to beta customers with explicit opt-in; collect cross-service header acceptance rate
Phase 3 (50->100%): wider rollout if no regressions. Gradual increase with automatic rollback on error-rate +5% or P95 latency regression >10%
Feature flagging in SDKs to allow per-call override and service-level disable via Console
Post-rollout: enable default on for new minor SDK releases after 30d of stable telemetry
